chunks: From him, from al-Abbas, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed Dhuhr and Asr, and he shortened the prayer in the last two rak'ahs. When he finished, the people said to him, 'O Messenger of Allah, did something new happen in the prayer?' He said, 'What is that?' They said, 'You shortened the last two rak'ahs.' So he said to them, 'Did you not hear the cry of the infant?'
ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet shorten the last two rak'ahs of Dhuhr and Asr?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of *mu'tamad* (following the needs of the congregation) in prayer, where the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) shortened the Dhuhr and Asr prayers due to the cry of an infant, demonstrating his attentiveness to the comfort of those behind him. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a primary evidence for the permissibility of shortening prayer durations (*taqdeer*) based on specific circumstances, such as the presence of children, the elderly, or the sick, rather than adhering strictly to a fixed duration. It highlights the Prophet's role as a shepherd who adjusts ritual practice to alleviate hardship for the community.
